what_its_for: Belumosudil is used to treat chronic graft-versus-host disease (cGVHD) in adults and children 12 years and older. This is a condition that can happen after a stem cell or bone marrow transplant, where the donated cells attack your body. This medicine is used when at least 2 other treatments have already been tried.
how_to_take: Take belumosudil by mouth as a tablet, once a day with a meal. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, cut, or chew it. Try to take it at the same time each day. If you vomit after taking your dose, do not take another dose that day — just take your next regular dose the following day.
dosing: The usual dose for adults and children 12 years and older is 200 mg (one tablet) taken by mouth once daily with food. Your doctor may adjust your dose if you are taking certain other medicines or if you have side effects. Always follow the dose your doctor prescribes.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. However, if it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store belumosudil tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the tablets in their original container with the cap tightly closed. Keep this medicine away from moisture, heat, and light. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine past the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids that contain aluminum or magnesium (such as Maalox or Mylanta) within 2 hours before or 2 hours after taking belumosudil, as they can lower the amount of medicine that gets into your body. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice, as they may affect how this medicine works. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before starting any new prescription medicines, over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, or herbal supplements, especially St. John's Wort, as they may interact with belumosudil.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience any of the following: shortness of breath, new or worsening cough, or chest pain (possible lung problems); signs of infection such as fever, chills, or feeling very unwell; severe nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or stomach pain; unusual tiredness or weakness; signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or pain in the upper right side of your belly; fast or irregular heartbeat; or any other new or concerning symptoms. Always let your doctor know about all medicines you are taking.
when_it_works: Belumosudil may start to improve your symptoms within a few weeks, but it may take several months to see the full benefit. Everyone responds differently, so stay in close contact with your doctor to track your progress. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel better.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Belumosudil can harm an unborn baby. If you can become pregnant, use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 1 week after the last dose. If you are a male with a female partner who can become pregnant, use contraception during treatment and for at least 1 week after the last dose. Do not breastfeed during treatment and for at least 1 week after the last dose. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted. Children: This medicine is not approved for children under 12 years of age. Older adults: No special dose adjustment is needed based on age alone, but your doctor will monitor you closely.
